findings.summary: Async exports run inline and can exhaust the request path
findings.details: triggerExport calls processExportJobAsync on the same service instance. With Spring proxy-based @Async, self-invocation is not intercepted, so the >1000-row path runs export generation before the POST can return 202. That same path fetches PageRequest.of(0, Integer.MAX_VALUE), so a large export can tie up the request transaction, time out, or run out of memory instead of behaving like a background job.
findings.tierReason: severity=high, confidence=0.92 (>=0.70), alreadyHandled=false — @Async self-invocation bypasses proxy; Integer.MAX_VALUE page load confirmed in code
findings.recommendation: Move export processing into a separate proxied bean, queue/event it after commit, and generate files by streaming or paging in bounded chunks rather than requesting Integer.MAX_VALUE rows.

findings.summary: Tenant-wide export contract is implemented as personal-only export
findings.details: The contract describes CLIENT_ADMIN exports with userId/companyId filters and ALL_TENANT scope, but TriggerExportRequest has no such fields and triggerExport always calls countPersonalHistory/findPersonalHistory for the caller and persists scope(PERSONAL). A client admin attempting a tenant-wide export will get only their own redemption rows, or a false 422 if they have none, which is a high-risk reporting/compliance data omission.
findings.tierReason: severity=high, confidence=0.95 (>=0.70), alreadyHandled=false — triggerExport hardcodes personal queries with no scope branching
findings.recommendation: Add explicit export scope plus admin-only userId/companyId filters to the request handling, authorize scope by permission, and route admin exports through tenant-history count/query methods while persisting the actual scope.

findings.summary: Company history drops redemptions from every company wallet except the first
findings.details: getCompanyHistory loads all COMPANY wallets for the caller partner company, then chooses companyWallets.get(0) and queries by that single wallet id. The schema supports one company wallet per currency, so any redemptions from the company other currency wallets disappear from company history without an error.
findings.tierReason: severity=medium — advisory regardless of confidence or alreadyHandled
findings.recommendation: Query company history by clientId and partnerCompanyId or by walletId IN (:walletIds), preserving pagination and sorting across all matching company wallets.

classificationRules.blockingThreshold: severity critical/high AND confidence >= 0.70 AND not alreadyHandled
classificationRules.advisoryThreshold: severity medium/low OR confidence < 0.70 OR alreadyHandled
